blocks.text: A charge placed in an electric field has electrical potential energy. If a charge qo is placed in the field of a charge q and allowed to move freely, it is repelled by q. Equation 16.17 shows that the potential falls with distance, so a positive charge free to move always accelerates from higher to lower potential. If the potential difference between these points is dV, the potential energy of the charge falls by dU = qo dV, and this loss appears as kinetic energy. For a body of mass m: (1/2) mv^2 = qo dV (16.18). A negative charge free to move goes from lower to higher potential.

Equation 16.18 shows that energy can be written as charge times potential difference. In atomic physics the electron volt (eV) is used: the energy gained by an electron accelerated through a potential difference of 1 volt. 1 eV = (charge on an electron) x 1 V = 1.6 x 10^-19 J.
Electric potential energy of two point charges

Consider two points A and B a distance r apart, with no field at first (Fig 16.4). Bring a charge Q from infinity to A: there is no field to oppose it, so the work done is WA = 0 (16.19). Q now creates a potential at B, V = (1/4 pi eo) Q / r (16.20). Bringing a second charge q from infinity to B needs work WB = qV (16.21) = (1/4 pi eo) Qq / r (16.22). The total work is W = WA + WB = (1/4 pi eo) Qq / r (16.23). By definition this work is stored as the electric potential energy of the pair: Ep = (1/4 pi eo) Qq / r (16.24).

blocks.alt: Two dashed paths come down from far away (infinity). Charge Q travels along one to point A, where VA = 0; charge q travels along the other to point B, where VB = V. A dashed arrow joins A to B.
blocks.caption: Figure 16.4: Charges Q and q brought from infinity to points A and B (printed in the book as Fig. 16.5; original drawing after the textbook's figure).

blocks.text: Two point charges of 8 uC and 5 uC are 4.0 cm apart. What is their electric potential energy? Solution: Ep = (1/4 pi eo) Qq / r = (9 x 10^9 N m^2 C^-2)(8 x 10^-6 C)(5 x 10^-6 C) / (4 x 10^-2 m) = 9 N m = 9 J.
